name: io.github.makinglyai/docket-room
title: Docket Room
description: Bills, hearings, votes and legislators for all 50 US states, DC and Congress, from official sources.

tools.name: search_bills
tools.description: Search bills across all 50 US states, DC, and Congress by keyword or bill number (e.g. 'HB 1032', 'SB0315', 'ai deepfakes'). Returns compact bill records with a docketroom.ai URL each.

tools.name: semantic_search_bills
tools.description: Meaning-based bill search: finds bills ABOUT a topic even when they don't share the query's words (e.g. 'algorithmic hiring discrimination' finds AI-employment bills). Use search_bills for exact keywords or bill numbers; use this for concepts, topics, and natural-language questions. Results are ordered by a hybrid rank (whole-bill + section-level matches fused), NOT by raw similarity — `rank` is the authoritative order; `similarity` (0-1) is informational and may not be monotonic.

query.description: Topic or natural-language description of the legislation you're looking for

tools.name: list_bills
tools.description: List bills filtered by state, status, topic tag, sponsor name, current committee, and/or date ranges (introduced/last-action), newest activity first.

tag.description: Topic filter — a slug or name from: agriculture, artificial-intelligence, budget-taxes, civil-rights, climate-environment, criminal-justice, defense-military, education, energy, foreign-policy, gun-policy, healthcare, housing, immigration, infrastructure, labor-employment, lgbtqplus, privacy-technology, social-security, voting-rights, women's-rights (e.g. 'artificial-intelligence' or 'Healthcare'). Matches bills whose text is about the topic; an unknown topic returns an error listing the valid ones.

committee.description: Committee name substring, e.g. 'Judiciary' — bills currently before that committee

last_action_after.description: ISO date — bills with activity since this date

tools.name: get_bill
tools.description: Get one bill with AI summaries, passage predictions, and linked hearings. Accepts a Docket Room id (from search_bills/list_bills) OR a natural reference like 'California SB 123' / 'US HR 1' — the most recently active matching session wins. detail='concise' returns just the identity/status/summary core when you don't need the full record.

id.description: Docket Room bill id (e.g. 'state-IN-2026-HB1032') or natural reference (e.g. 'California SB 123')

tools.name: get_bill_votes
tools.description: Get roll-call vote tallies for a bill: per roll call, yes/no/not-voting counts with a party split. Covers Congress plus states with member-level votes (e.g. IN, MA).

tools.name: list_bill_versions
tools.description: A bill's stored text versions in chronological order (1 = introduced). Version tracking covers federal bills; compare pairs with compare_bill_versions.

tools.name: compare_bill_versions
tools.description: Structured amendment analysis between two versions of a bill (defaults: the latest pair): what was added/removed/modified, each change classified substantive vs technical and categorized (penalty, scope, enforcement, effective_date, coverage, definitions, appropriations), with verbatim quotes re-verified against the correct version's text. First call generates (~1 min); cached afterward.

tools.name: analyze_bill
tools.description: Structured AI analysis of a bill: covered entities, requirements/prohibitions/exemptions/penalties, effective dates, enforcement agencies, and ambiguous language. Each item carries a verbatim quote re-verified against the bill text — verified=true means the exact language exists in the bill; verified=false marks model interpretation. First call generates (may take ~1 minute); repeat calls are cached.

refresh.description: Force regeneration even if a cached analysis exists

tools.name: get_bill_text
tools.description: The bill's original legislative text (as ingested, not a summary), chunked — request further chunks via offset. Use get_bill first; reach for full text only when the analysis needs exact statutory language.

tools.name: get_bill_cosponsors
tools.description: The full cosponsor list for a bill (get_bill carries only the count). legislator_id links to list_legislators results when resolved.

tools.name: related_bills
tools.description: Bills similar to a given bill by embedding similarity — companions, copied/model legislation, and same-topic bills in other states. Set exclude_same_state=true to survey how OTHER jurisdictions handle the same subject.

tools.name: compare_bills
tools.description: Multistate comparison matrix: how different jurisdictions regulate the same subject. Pass bill_ids (2-8) to compare specific bills, or a topic (+ optional states) to survey — one best-matching bill per state. Returns a per-jurisdiction compliance matrix (scope, obligations, enforcement, penalties, exemptions, effective dates — every item quote-verified against that bill's text), a comparative synthesis (normalized terminology, strictest/most-lenient jurisdiction, conflicting requirements, outliers, common trends), and an embedding-based model-legislation report (shared/copied language at ≥0.9 similarity). First uncached call can take ~1-2 min; repeats are cached.

bill_ids.description: Docket Room bill ids to compare (2-8)

topic.description: Topic to survey across jurisdictions, e.g. 'ai deepfakes in elections'

states.description: With topic: limit the survey to these states (US for Congress)

max_states.description: With topic and no states: jurisdiction cap

tools.name: bill_momentum
tools.description: Is this bill gaining or losing momentum? A deterministic score over the bill's detected activity in the trailing 7 days (status advances, amendments, upcoming hearings, sponsor changes, actions — each signal named with its point contribution), direction vs the bill's own prior 30-day rate, a fast-mover flag, and the bill's prediction history (probability snapshots over time with mechanical trend). Scores are activity tallies, not outcome guarantees.

tools.name: fast_movers
tools.description: Bills that require immediate attention: the most legislative activity detected in the window (default 7 days), highest momentum first, each with the per-signal breakdown behind its score (status changes weigh 5, amendments 4, upcoming hearings 3, sponsor changes 2, actions 1 — capped per type). Filter by state. Momentum is a mechanical activity tally, not an outcome prediction.

tools.name: list_legislators
tools.description: List current legislators, filterable by state, chamber, party, or name.

tools.name: get_legislator
tools.description: One legislator's full profile: contact + office details, committee memberships with leadership roles (federal members carry full assignments; state memberships are not yet ingested), sponsorship history with derived issue areas, and recent sponsored bills.

tools.name: legislators_on_topic
tools.description: Which lawmakers are active on a policy topic: sponsors of topic-matching bills ranked by how many they sponsor, each with sample bills. Use get_legislator on the top results for full profiles.

tools.name: bill_stakeholders
tools.description: The stakeholder map for a bill: a FACTUAL assembly (sponsor + cosponsor party split, committees of jurisdiction with federal rosters and leadership, roll-call party splits, hearing witnesses with their organizations, enforcement agencies from the bill's analysis) plus an AI likely-supporters/opponents/swing synthesis grounded only in those facts. First call generates the synthesis (~30s); cached until the underlying facts change.

skip_analysis.description: true → facts only, no AI synthesis

tools.name: upcoming_hearings
tools.description: Legislative hearings calendar: upcoming committee hearings across all 50 states + Congress, soonest first. Filter by state, a specific bill, or tracked=true (OAuth) for hearings on the signed-in user's tracked bills — 'what hearings are coming up on my bills this week?'.

bill_id.description: Only hearings linked to this Docket Room bill id

tracked.description: Only hearings on the signed-in user's tracked bills (requires OAuth)

tools.name: get_hearing
tools.description: One hearing with full detail: committee, date, location, status, access details (video/stream + transcript links), listed witnesses, and the bills on its agenda.

tools.name: hearing_brief
tools.description: AI hearing-preparation brief: overview, logistics, per-bill agenda with key provisions, likely themes and questions, witnesses to watch, and prep recommendations — composed from the hearing's ingested notice, its linked bills, and their quote-verified analyses. First call generates (~1 min); cached until the hearing or its bills change.

tools.name: search_regulations
tools.description: Federal rulemaking (Federal Register): search proposed and final rules by keyword and agency. Keyword queries rank by relevance (websearch syntax: quotes for phrases, - to negate). Set open_for_comment=true for rules whose public comment window is still open (deadline-ordered when no query is given).

open_for_comment.description: Only rules currently accepting public comments

tools.name: get_regulation
tools.description: One regulation with full detail (abstract, agencies, comment deadline, Federal Register link) and its related bills.

id.description: Docket Room regulation id (fedreg-…) or a Federal Register document number

tools.name: recent_changes
tools.description: What changed in the legislature: field-level bill changes (new actions, status changes, new bills, sponsor/cosponsor changes, amendments, hearing scheduled/rescheduled/cancelled) detected by the nightly ingest, newest first. Filter by state, change type, and 'since' (ISO date, default 7 days back, max 90).

materiality.description: material = status changes, amendments, hearings, new bills; procedural = routine actions and sponsor shifts

since.description: ISO date OR full ISO timestamp — sub-day windows work, e.g. 2026-07-01 or 2026-07-28T14:30:00Z (default: 7 days back)

tools.name: activity_summary
tools.description: What changed since yesterday / Friday / last week: the change feed GROUPED BY BILL with material developments (status changes, substantive amendments, hearing events, new bills) separated from routine procedural activity, and the bills needing attention ranked first. Set tracked=true (OAuth) for the signed-in user's tracked bills; narrative=true adds a short AI briefing composed strictly over the digest. Works for any window — daily, weekly, or session-to-date.

since.description: ISO date OR full ISO timestamp (sub-day windows work, e.g. 2026-07-28T14:30:00Z; default: 1 day back, max 90 days)

tracked.description: Only the signed-in user's tracked bills (requires OAuth)

narrative.description: Add an AI catch-up briefing over the digest

tools.name: get_bill_changes
tools.description: One bill's detected change history (actions, status, sponsors), newest first.

since.description: ISO date OR full ISO timestamp (sub-day windows work; default: 7 days back, max 90 days)

tools.name: bill_timeline
tools.description: A bill's full dated history from Docket Room's records, newest first: every official action, the status changes and amendments the nightly detected, text versions and hearings, with the events that moved the bill flagged material=true. Free plans see the latest 3 events.

id.description: Docket Room bill id or natural reference, e.g. 'TX SB 1188'

material_only.description: Only events that moved the bill (passage, signature, veto, committee votes, amendments, status changes, hearings)

tools.name: verify_quote
tools.description: Check whether exact language appears in a bill's text, and where. Returns the passage as printed, its section, which text version was checked and whether that is the final (enrolled) version — or, when it isn't there, the closest passage and how similar it is. Use before quoting a bill to a client. Free plans get 5 checks a day.

id.description: Docket Room bill id or natural reference, e.g. 'TX SB 1188'

tools.name: tracked_changes
tools.description: What changed on the bills the signed-in user tracks — the personal monitoring digest. Requires an OAuth connection.

since.description: ISO date OR full ISO timestamp (sub-day windows work; default: 7 days back, max 90 days)

tools.name: whats_new
tools.description: The morning check: what changed on the signed-in user's tracked bills and keyword alerts since they last called whats_new, plus hearings on tracked bills in the next 7 days. Docket Room remembers when you last asked, so the user never has to say 'since when'. Requires an OAuth connection.

since.description: Override the starting point: ISO date or timestamp (max 90 days back). Default: the previous whats_new call, or 7 days on the first call.

peek.description: Look without moving the 'last asked' point (default false)

tools.name: set_alerts
tools.description: View or change the signed-in user's alert settings: the email digest (on/off, daily or weekly, hour and time zone), hearing alerts and their lead time, status-change alerts, and how often each tracked bill or keyword alert notifies. Docket Room checks bills nightly, so alerts arrive in the digest, not instantly. Call with no arguments to see the current settings. Requires an OAuth connection.

hearing_lead_time_hours.description: How far ahead of a hearing to alert

bills.description: Per tracked bill: urgent_only, daily, weekly or never

tools.name: generate_report
tools.description: Composed legislative report, audience-tailored: executive_briefing (what a decision-maker must know), issue_report (the landscape on a topic), or risk_summary (leadership-ready exposure ranking). Subject = bill_ids (up to 8 used) or a topic survey; set tracked bill ids from list_tracked_bills for a portfolio report. Returns the structured report AND a markdown rendering; bill references are validated against the source appendix. Composes over stored data + cached analyses only — run analyze_bill on key bills first for richer inputs. First call generates (~30-60s); cached afterward.

audience.description: Who this is for, e.g. 'board of directors', 'general counsel', 'client: mid-size fintech'

topic.description: Survey a topic instead of naming bills

state.description: With topic: limit the survey to one state

tools.name: list_webhooks
tools.description: The team's outbound webhook subscriptions: each receives one HMAC-signed batch of matching bill changes after the nightly ingest (empty batches are never sent). Delivery health (last status, consecutive failures, auto-disable) is included.

tools.name: create_webhook
tools.description: Create an outbound webhook for the team: a daily HMAC-signed POST of bill changes matching the filter (payload mirrors /v1/changes rows; signature = 'sha256=' + HMAC-SHA256(secret, raw body) in X-DocketRoom-Signature). The signing secret is returned ONCE — store it. A test ping fires immediately and its result is returned (the URL must answer 2xx). HTTPS public hosts only.

materiality.description: material = status changes, amendments, hearings, new bills only

tools.name: delete_webhook
tools.description: Delete one of the team's webhook subscriptions (by id from list_webhooks). This is the reversal path for webhook delivery — no further batches are sent. Confirm with the user before deleting.

tools.name: get_organization_profile
tools.description: The team's organization profile (industry, products, jurisdictions, activities, priorities) — the context assess_bill_impact and scan_relevant_bills personalize against.

tools.name: set_organization_profile
tools.description: Create or update the team's organization profile. Provided fields are updated; omitted fields keep their current value. The richer the profile, the better relevance and impact assessments get.

description.description: What the organization does, in plain English

activities.description: Business activities with regulatory exposure, e.g. 'collects consumer location data; operates delivery fleets'

priorities.description: Policy priorities/sensitivities, e.g. 'privacy preemption, gig-worker classification'

risk_tolerance.description: How conservatively impact assessments should flag severity (#118)

tools.name: assess_bill_impact
tools.description: Assess a bill against the team's organization profile: is it relevant, why, which operations it touches, legal/financial/operational/reputational severity, concrete compliance obligations (quote-verified against the bill text), and recommended questions for legal/policy review. First call generates (~1 min); cached until the bill text or profile changes.

tools.name: scan_relevant_bills
tools.description: Find bills relevant to the team's organization even when they don't use expected keywords: profile facets (industry, products, activities, priorities) become semantic queries over the embedding index; results are FILTERED to the profile's jurisdictions (state overrides; empty jurisdictions = nationwide), deduped, ranked by similarity + legislative recency, and each match says which facet found it. Follow up with assess_bill_impact on the top hits.

state.description: Limit to one state (US for Congress)

tools.name: set_team_bill_record
tools.description: Create or update the TEAM's working record on a bill (kept strictly separate from official legislative facts and from personal tracking): owner, organizational position (support/oppose/support_with_amendment/neutral/watch — SHARED with the team's app workspace, including its Slack notifications), priority, internal status, recommended next steps. Provided fields update; omitted fields keep their value. Confirm with the user before changing an existing position. Changes are written to the team audit history.

id.description: Docket Room bill id or natural reference

owner.description: Team member responsible (name or email — recorded as given)

internal_status.description: Free-form workflow state, e.g. 'legal review', 'awaiting board'

tools.name: add_team_bill_note
tools.description: Append an internal note to the TEAM's record on a bill (notes are append-only, shared with the team's app workspace, and never mixed with official legislative facts). Confirm with the user before posting on their behalf.

id.description: Docket Room bill id or natural reference

tools.name: get_team_bill_record
tools.description: The TEAM's working record on a bill — organizational position (shared with the app workspace), owner, priority, internal status, recommended actions — plus its append-only notes and the audit history of record changes (#107). Internal context only; official legislative facts come from get_bill.

id.description: Docket Room bill id or natural reference

tools.name: list_team_bill_records
tools.description: All bills the TEAM keeps a working record or organizational position on, most recently updated first — the team's shared docket (same state the app workspace shows). Filter by position or owner substring.

owner.description: Substring match on the owner name

tools.name: set_bill_relevance
tools.description: Record the team's HUMAN verdict on a bill's relevance — it overrides the model: 'not_relevant' bills stop appearing in scan_relevant_bills and the override is echoed on assess_bill_impact; 'relevant' confirms and annotates. Pass clear=true to remove the override and let the model judge again.

tools.name: track_bill
tools.description: Track a bill for the signed-in user (adds it to their Docket Room tracked list, enabling change alerts). Requires an OAuth connection — team API keys carry no user identity.

tools.name: untrack_bill
tools.description: Stop tracking a bill for the signed-in user. Requires an OAuth connection. Confirm with the user before untracking.

tools.name: update_tracked_bill
tools.description: Set the signed-in user's organizational position and/or priority on a bill they track. Requires an OAuth connection.

tools.name: list_keyword_alerts
tools.description: The signed-in user's keyword/issue monitors (each scans new legislative activity and alerts on matches). Requires an OAuth connection.

tools.name: create_keyword_alert
tools.description: Create a keyword/issue monitor for the signed-in user: new bills and activity matching the keyword trigger alerts (issue-based monitoring across jurisdictions). Requires an OAuth connection.

keyword.description: Keyword or phrase to monitor, e.g. 'deepfake'

context.description: Disambiguation context, e.g. 'AI-generated media, not fraud'

tools.name: delete_keyword_alert
tools.description: Delete one of the signed-in user's keyword monitors (by id from list_keyword_alerts). Requires an OAuth connection. Confirm with the user before deleting.

tools.name: list_tracked_bills
tools.description: List the bills the signed-in user tracks, most recently tracked first. Requires an OAuth connection.
